summary.text: Michael Whatley is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat in North Carolina. A lawyer and longtime Republican operative who has not held elective office, he served as chief of staff to Sen. Elizabeth Dole, worked in energy-industry advocacy, chaired the North Carolina Republican Party from 2019 and the Republican National Committee from 2024 to 2025. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 64.6% of the vote and is endorsed by President Trump.

paragraphs.text: Whatley says he was raised in Blowing Rock, the son of an accountant and a librarian, and graduated from Watauga High School.
As a high school student he volunteered for Sen. Jesse Helms's 1984 re-election campaign.

He earned a bachelor's degree in history from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte in 1991, a master's degree in religion from Wake Forest University in 1993, a master's degree in theology from the University of Notre Dame in 1994 and a law degree from Notre Dame Law School in 1997, according to Ballotpedia.
Whatley began his career as a federal law clerk in Charlotte, and Ballotpedia reports he was legal counsel to Sen. Paul Coverdell (R-Ga.) in 2000.
He worked on George W. Bush's Florida recount team in 2000 and, from 2001 to 2003, was a principal deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Energy under Bush.
In 2004 Sen. Elizabeth Dole named him her chief of staff.

Whatley was an executive vice president of the Consumer Energy Alliance from 2007 to 2019 and a partner at the lobbying firm HBW Resources, which The Assembly describes as a lobbying firm for oil and gas companies.
After President Trump's 2016 victory he led the Presidential Transition's energy, environment and agriculture teams, according to his campaign website.
Party leaders elected him chair of the North Carolina Republican Party in June 2019, and the Republican National Committee elected him its chair on March 8, 2024.
He resigned as RNC chair on August 22, 2025, after announcing his Senate run.
Whatley's campaign says he and his wife Suzanne live in Gaston County and have three children.
